Network Segments

The installation-wide list of named networks a new server policy puts its VIP on. Each segment holds one or more networks (CIDR, gateway, optional interface) tried in order when IPAM assigns the address, and is scoped to a zone, line and departments.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb, FortiAnalyzer or FortiAuthenticator ADOM → Administrator → Network Segments (URL /segments/)

ℹ️Note

New: a segment holds one or more networks. When the VIP is reserved from IPAM it is taken from the first network with a free address, then the next — the operator no longer picks which. See Several networks in one segment.

What is it?#

Network Segments is the registry of the networks new server policies put their VIP on. Each segment has a name, one or more networks (a CIDR and its gateway, optionally the appliance interface that reaches it), a default interface, and can be scoped to a zone, a line and one or more departments from the Classification catalogs. When a new server policy is built from a line, the wizard reserves (or checks) the VIP in the networks of the segment that line receives and binds the VIP to that network's interface.

What does it do?#

  • Keeps one list of segments for the whole SATOM installation (it is not per ADOM).
  • Validates every CIDR, refuses two segments with the same name and refuses the same CIDR twice in one segment.
  • Gives the new-policy wizard the networks to reserve the VIP from, in order, and the interface to put it on.
  • Feeds the segment choice of a line: Line profiles name segments explicitly; without a profile, SATOM falls back to the segments whose Line equals the line name.
  • Lets other pages group appliances by segment: an appliance belongs to the segment one of whose networks contains its management address (used by Bookmarks and ADOM asset views; addresses outside every segment show as (no segment)).
  • Shows a segment count and IP totals (every network counted) on the Analysis dashboard, filtered by the zone/line/department in view.

Requirements#

  • Zones, lines and departments are defined on the Classification page. The segment form offers them as choices; a blank value means any.
  • Nothing needs to be registered on an appliance first — segments are SATOM data, not device configuration.

Permissions#

All routes require users.manage (Administrator). Without it, /segments/ answers 403 and the menu entry is not shown (the Administrator menu group is drawn only for users.manage).

Where it is reachable.

ADOM Behaviour
FortiWeb Administrator → Network Segments
FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator Administrator → Network Segments
Global No menu entry; opening the URL switches the tab to the FortiWeb ADOM
FortiADC Not reachable; the URL redirects to the FortiADC home page

The page is also linked from the Line Profiles page (Network segments button).

How to use#

Add or edit segments#

  1. Open Administrator → Network Segments.
  2. Check the Classification reference card for the zones, lines and departments available. To change them, press Edit catalogs.
  3. Press Add segment to add an empty row, or edit an existing row in place.
  4. Fill in Name, the Interface (pre-filled port1 on a new row; used by every network that does not name its own) and an optional Note.
  5. Under Networks, fill in the CIDR and gateway of the first network. Press Add network for each further one, and leave its interface blank unless that network is reached through another port. The order shown is the order addresses are taken in; the × removes a network.
  6. Choose a Zone and a Line (— any — for no restriction), and select one or more Departments in the multi-select. A network shared by two departments is one row with both selected.
  7. Press Save Segments.

Several networks in one segment#

When the line's segment has more than one network:

  • IPAM reserves the VIP (wizard option Reserve the VIP from IPAM): the address comes from the first network with a free address. If IPAM refuses one — full, or any other error — the next is tried. The address step of the run names every network that refused and why, and the preview shows the order (would take the next free address from A, then B if it has none free).
  • A network no IPAM backend can serve (no backend claims it, a tie, an unreachable backend) is shown as a warning, this network will NOT be tried. The plan blocks only when no network can be used.
  • The VIP is bound to the interface of the network it came from, and if a later step fails the address is released back to that network.
  • A VIP typed by hand must sit in one of the segment's networks, or the plan is blocked with address_not_in_segment. A VIP written with its mask ({ip}/24) is accepted.
  • The gateway is stored with each network for reference; no SATOM flow writes it to the device.
  • A line profile that names an explicit IPAM pool still uses that pool alone.

Remove a segment#

  1. Press the trash button at the end of the row. The row disappears from the form.
  2. Press Save Segments. The saved list is exactly what the form holds.

⚠️Warning — Removing a segment a line still needs

A Line profile that names a segment you deleted reports "segment '' is named by this line but no longer exists in Network segments", and the new-policy wizard treats it as a problem rather than a shorter list.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Identifies the network. Must be unique (exact, case-sensitive comparison). Line profiles refer to segments by this name. Yes, unless only a CIDR is given web-dmz
Zone Classification zone the segment belongs to; — any — = no restriction No dmz
Line Classification line; used to infer segments for a line that has no line profile No public-web
Departments Any number of classification departments No sales, support
Networks → CIDR Network in CIDR notation, IPv4 or IPv6; host bits are allowed and the value is stored as typed. One row per network, in allocation order. No (but a line plan reports a segment without any CIDR as a problem) 192.0.2.0/24
Networks → gateway Gateway address for that network No 192.0.2.1
Networks → interface Interface for that network only; blank = the segment's Interface No port4
Interface Appliance interface of every network that does not name its own. Saved as port1 when left blank. No port2
Note Free text No Front-end web servers

A value that is no longer in the classification catalog stays selected and is marked (custom).

Example#

🧪Example — Two departments on one network

Sales and Support both publish services from 198.51.100.0/24, reached through port3.

Name Zone Line Departments Networks Interface
shared-apps internal intranet sales, support 198.51.100.0/24 gw 198.51.100.1 port3

Create one row and select both departments. A second row named shared-apps would be refused on save.

🧪Example — A segment that grows a second network

web-dmz started as {ip}/24 on port3 and is nearly full. Add a second network {ip}/24, gateway {ip}, interface port9. New policies keep taking addresses from {ip}/24 while it has any; after that IPAM refuses it, the wizard takes the next free address of {ip}/24 and binds the VIP to port9.

Result#

  • The list is saved as a whole and the page shows " network segment(s) saved."
  • The Audit log records segments.save with the number of segments.
  • Line plans, the new-policy wizard, the Analysis dashboard and appliance grouping use the new list immediately.
  • Renaming or removing a zone, line or department on the Classification page updates the segments that use it; removing a value still used by segments asks you to decide what happens to them first.

Troubleshooting#

"two or more segments share the name(s) '…' — a segment name identifies one network, so add the extra department to the existing row instead of adding a second row."#

Possible causes - Two rows carry the same name.

Solution 1. Merge the rows: keep one, select all its departments, delete the other. 2. Or give the second network a different name. 3. Press Save Segments.

Verification - The success message appears. Nothing was written by the refused save — the previous list is still in place, so re-enter the edits you made.

"Skipped invalid CIDR(s): …"#

Possible causes - A CIDR is not a valid IPv4/IPv6 network (for example 192.0.2.0/33).

Solution 1. Only the networks with an invalid CIDR were dropped; the segment and its other networks were saved. Add the network again with a valid CIDR. 2. Press Save Segments.

Verification - The network is present after reload and the warning does not appear.

"a segment lists the same network twice (…) — keep one entry per CIDR."#

Possible causes - Two networks of one segment carry the same CIDR.

Solution 1. Remove one of them (keep the one with the right gateway) and press Save Segments. Nothing was written by the refused save.

A line gets no segments, or the wrong ones#

Possible causes - The line has no line profile and no segment's Line equals the line name exactly. - The line profile names a segment that was renamed or deleted.

Solution 1. Declare the line's segments on Line profiles, or set the Line of the right segments here.

Verification - The line profile shows its segments without a missing segment problem.

Advanced#

Advanced Storage and parsing

Segments are stored as one JSON list in SATOM's application settings. The form posts every column as a parallel list; departments and networks each travel as one JSON-encoded value per row so a variable-length list cannot shift the other columns. Each segment keeps a networks list; its single cidr and gateway fields mirror the first network, so readers written for one network still read it. Rows with neither a name nor a network are dropped. Older data with a single department value is read as a one-item department list, and a segment saved before networks existed is read as one network made of its cidr and gateway.

#network segment#cidr#subnet#interface#gateway#vip#ipam#several networks#multiple cidr#zone#line#department#classification
